examples: There is a cat in our house.
nuance: 고양이 is the everyday word for a cat, and people often call a kitten 아기 고양이. Owners may also use the cute nickname 냥이.
mistakes: Saying 고양이를 있어요 instead of 고양이가 있어요

examples: There is a bird in the tree.
The bird sings in the morning.
nuance: 새 is a short one syllable word for any bird in general. To name a specific bird Koreans add a word, like 참새 for sparrow.
mistakes: Confusing 새 the bird with 새 meaning new

examples: There is a fish in the tank.
nuance: 물고기 is a live swimming fish, while fish prepared to eat is 생선. Use 물고기 for a pond or tank, not for a restaurant order.
mistakes: Saying 물고기 when ordering fish to eat

examples: There is a rabbit in the park.
The child looks at the rabbit.
nuance: 토끼 means a rabbit and also appears in the famous moon story where a rabbit pounds rice cakes. Children learn it very early.
mistakes: Adding a plural ending because English says rabbits

examples: There is a bear at the zoo.
nuance: 곰 ends in a consonant so it takes 이 not 가 as the subject marker. A teddy bear is called 곰 인형 in everyday speech.
mistakes: Saying 곰가 있어요 instead of 곰이 있어요

examples: There is a tiger at the zoo.
nuance: 호랑이 appears in many Korean folk tales and often opens stories with 옛날 옛날에. It is felt as a powerful and famous animal.
mistakes: Dropping a syllable and saying 호랑 instead of 호랑이

usage: I look at the lion too
examples: There is a lion at the zoo.
nuance: 사자 is the word for a lion and is mostly seen at the zoo or on television. The same sounds can mean other words, so context matters.
mistakes: Using 호랑이 when you actually mean 사자

examples: There is an elephant at the zoo.
The child looks at the elephant.
nuance: 코끼리 starts with 코 which means nose, a nice hint for its long trunk. It is a favorite animal for young children at the zoo.
mistakes: Saying 코끼리를 있어요 instead of 코끼리가 있어요

examples: There is a horse on the farm.
I want to ride a horse.
nuance: 말 also means speech or words, so the same sound has two meanings. Pitch and context tell you which 말 a speaker means.
mistakes: Confusing 말 the horse with 말 meaning speech

usage: I look at the pig too
examples: There is a pig on the farm.
nuance: 돼지 is the animal pig, while its meat is 돼지고기. Seeing a pig in a dream is thought to bring good luck in Korea.
mistakes: Saying 돼지 when you mean the meat 돼지고기

examples: There is a chicken on the farm.
The chicken crows in the morning.
nuance: 닭 is the live chicken, while fried chicken to eat is usually called 치킨. The final consonant cluster makes it sound like 닥 when spoken.
mistakes: Saying 닭 when you mean fried chicken 치킨

examples: There is a puppy in our house.
nuance: 강아지 means a puppy but Koreans often call any pet dog 강아지 with affection. The plain word for a grown dog is 개.
mistakes: Using 강아지 in formal writing where 개 is expected
